definitions.meaning: a piece on the chess board, the one shaped like a horse
a mounted warrior who fought on behalf of a lord or lady

explanation.surface: A title for the winner of a chess tournament.
explanation.definitionFit: The horse-headed chess piece carries this name, and a medieval armoured fighter who defended a cause was also one.

parts.note: a twist on the phrase 'hot and bothered', so staying calm and also chilled

explanation.surface: Advice to stay calm.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for staying calm and composed under pressure.

clue.text: Told, but possibly not needing to be

definitions.text: Told, but possibly not needing to be

parts.words: Told, but possibly not needing to be
parts.note: someone given news, though a person already knowledgeable would not need the telling

explanation.surface: Someone given information they may already have had.
explanation.definitionFit: Having been given the facts, or being well-read and knowledgeable already.

clue.text: Such resolution makes for a clear picture

definitions.text: Such resolution makes for a clear picture

parts.words: Such resolution makes for a clear picture
parts.note: resolution here is the sharpness of a screen image, not a New Year promise

explanation.surface: Determination helps you see things clearly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolution' looks like firm intent; in imaging it is detail level, and a sharp picture comes from a lot of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A screen or photo with great detail is described as being of this level of resolution.

clue.text: Progressing rapidly getting fit on holiday

parts.note: fit means healthy, in good shape
someone on holiday is not at home

explanation.surface: Someone recovering fast after a restorative break.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for being well advanced, making good headway on a task.

clue.text: Moroccan pub crawl for the rock musician?

definitions.text: Moroccan pub crawl for the rock musician?

parts.words: Moroccan pub crawl for the rock musician?
parts.note: a pub crawl taking in that number of bars, with a Rif (a Moroccan Berber) on the trip, gives a guitarist's repeated phrase

explanation.surface: A rock star touring the drinking spots of Morocco.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rif are a Berber people of northern Morocco; a riff is a short repeated pattern in rock music, and an eight-bar one spans eight measures.
explanation.definitionFit: A short repeated musical phrase lasting that many measures, a staple of rock guitar.

clue.text: Still to come, or already gone?

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone is yet to arrive or has left.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means behind schedule and also recently deceased, as in 'the late king'.

parts.note: taken as written
er is a short sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Turning down an offer almost without pause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decline' suggests refusing, but here it means fade or shrivel.
explanation.definitionFit: To shrivel, droop or fade away, as plants do without water.

parts.note: off-peak suggests cheap phone rates, but it means singing calls from Alpine mountains

explanation.surface: Phoning at cheap times while in Switzerland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off-peak' looks like a cheap-rate phone time; here it means calling off the peak of a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpine herders sing in a warbling call switching between chest voice and falsetto.

parts.note: a model of a person, of the kind thrown on a bonfire in protest or on Guy Fawkes Night

explanation.surface: A puzzle-like hint about something that ends up on a fire.
explanation.walkthrough: On Bonfire Night in Britain (5 November) a stuffed model of Guy Fawkes is burnt; protesters likewise burn models of hated leaders.
explanation.definitionFit: A dummy or likeness of a person, traditionally set alight as a protest or celebration.

explanation.surface: Someone rattled and distressed after a bad experience.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both stirring a liquid vigorously and being nervously disturbed.

clue.text: One would offer a seat to such a friend!

definitions.text: One would offer a seat to such a friend!

parts.words: One would offer a seat to such a friend!
parts.note: an old friend is one of many years, but read literally one who has been on their feet a long time

explanation.surface: Courtesy to a dear old companion.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes something that has lasted for many years, as an established friendship has.

clue.text: Copper about to undergo a course of treatment

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A police officer about to go through medical therapy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a policeman, but here it is the metal, giving its symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A remedy or regime of medicine meant to restore health.

parts.note: a nod to the phrase about news spread by people talking rather than in print

explanation.surface: Gossip passed along through talk.
explanation.definitionFit: News that spreads by 'word of' this body part is passed on orally between people.

definitions.meaning: a plank of pine or fir timber
to buy and sell, do business

explanation.surface: A government department that oversees commerce.
explanation.walkthrough: The Board of Trade was a British government body; here the phrase splits into two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means softwood timber planks and also to do business or bargain.

indicators.note: sound tells us to use a word that is said the same way as the synonym

parts.note: to require is to need

explanation.surface: Needing a proper rubdown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like an adjective meaning good, but it signals a homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: Working dough or muscles by pressing and squeezing with the hands.

clue.text: She goes round in a radiant glow

indicators.note: goes round means the woman's word encircles the other piece

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman twirling, lit up with happiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She' reads as a person in the surface, but its letters are used as written; 'goes round' is the container signal and 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A bright gleam or lustre, the light given off by a polished surface.

parts.note: the 'deep' here is the sea, so this is the science of the sea

explanation.surface: Intense concentration on something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deep study' looks like hard concentration; 'the deep' is a poetic name for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The scientific discipline examining seas and their currents, life and floors.

clue.text: Words are not about to stick

indicators.note: about here means the contraction is put around the adhesive

parts.note: aren't is short for are not
gum is glue, something that sticks

explanation.surface: Words that fail to stick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Words' means a quarrel, as in having words with someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Having 'words' with someone is a quarrel or heated dispute.

clue.text: Impact he made in strong terms

indicators.note: made suggests the letters are formed into something new

parts.note: anagram fodder, as written

explanation.surface: The impression a man left by speaking forcefully.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoken forcefully and decisively, with clear stress laid on the point.

parts.note: read literally, something that smashes gates, a siege weapon

explanation.surface: An uninvited party guest.
explanation.walkthrough: A gate-crasher is usually an uninvited guest; here it is a device that literally crashes through a castle gate.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy log used in sieges to break down doors and gates.

clue.text: Tease about record of Mary's husband

indicators.note: about shows the teasing word wraps round the disc

parts.note: to josh is to tease playfully
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Teasing someone about a recording of the Virgin Mary's spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Gospels the carpenter of Nazareth was wedded to the mother of Jesus.

indicators.note: out means the letters of points are knocked out of their order

parts.note: anagram fodder, as written

explanation.surface: Someone noting equipment useful for mountaineering.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal spikes driven into rock cracks to secure a rope when mountaineering.

clue.text: Party back in power in old Scandinavia

indicators.note: back tells us to read the party word from right to left

parts.note: a do is a party
taken as written

explanation.surface: A political party returning to government in ancient Norway or Sweden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns DO into OD. 'power' is not a political force but a deity.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief Norse god, a divine force worshipped by the old Norse peoples.

clue.text: At a pinch it may be used as a sedative

definitions.text: At a pinch it may be used as a sedative

parts.words: At a pinch it may be used as a sedative
parts.note: powdered tobacco is taken in pinches, and to put out a candle is to quieten it

explanation.surface: Something taken in an emergency to calm the nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At a pinch' seems to mean 'if need be', but powdered tobacco is literally taken by the pinch.
explanation.definitionFit: Powdered tobacco sniffed up the nose, taken a pinch at a time.

definitions.meaning: uncultivated country, especially in Australia or Africa
the surname of two former US presidents

explanation.surface: A former head of state with an untamed reputation.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a name for scrubland or outback and the surname of two US presidents, father and son.

indicators.note: in a down clue upwards means the little word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: CI is 101 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: More than a hundred and one places where people gather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upwards of' looks like 'more than', but 'Upwards' turns OF into FO.
explanation.definitionFit: Central points where lines or rays converge, the plural of a focal point.

parts.note: levels here are floors of a building, so something running between storeys

explanation.surface: Something that works on several planes.
explanation.definitionFit: An elevator carries people between floors of a building.

clue.text: With new income around the company becomes profitable

indicators.note: around means the reworked letters wrap the company abbreviation
new tells us the letters of income are made over into a fresh order

parts.note: anagram fodder, as written

explanation.surface: A firm whose fresh earnings put it in the black.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' is the anagram signal, giving ENOMIC; 'around' is the container signal; 'With' and 'becomes' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that pays its way or brings a financial return is commercially viable.

indicators.note: provided suggests the letters of credit are supplied in a different form

parts.note: anagram fodder, as written

explanation.surface: Instant credit being made available.
explanation.walkthrough: 'provided' is an unusual anagram signal: the letters of CREDIT are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Without anything intervening, as in a straight, unmediated link.

clue.text: Strange things about American election campaigns

indicators.note: about shows the jumbled letters going round the abbreviation
strange suggests the letters of things are oddly jumbled

parts.note: anagram fodder, as written

explanation.surface: Odd goings-on concerning a person from the States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' is the anagram signal, giving HTINGS; 'about' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Political canvassing and speeches before a vote; originally the platform where candidates spoke.

definitions.meaning: the charge that builds up on surfaces and makes hair stand on end

explanation.surface: A steady kind of electrical power.
explanation.definitionFit: Means unmoving or fixed, and also the electric charge built up by friction.
